checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that the 'Horizontal swimming posture' checkpoint is missing; the diver is clearly in a vertical orientation facing the camera. All other equipment and anatomical checkpoints (mask, regulator, wetsuit, BCD, tank, fins) are correctly marked as present. The Router was accurate in its assessment of testability and presence for all items.
artifact_review: The Router identified texture anomalies in the right hand (fused fingers) and structural issues with the regulator hose connection. I agree with these findings. Additionally, visual inspection reveals significant artifacts in the left hand (viewer's right), which appears malformed with indistinct, fused digits rather than a natural grip or open hand. The fin on the right side of the image also exhibits structural ambiguity, appearing to merge with the water background without a clear boot/foot connection point. The severity of the hand artifacts is consistent with the Router's rating, but the presence of defects in *both* hands suggests a systemic generation issue with extremities.
alignment_reasoning: 8 out of 9 checkpoints passed. The single failure is the pose orientation (vertical vs horizontal), which is a definitive mismatch with the taxonomy. Equipment rendering is otherwise high-fidelity.
artifact_reasoning: Router correctly flagged right hand fusion and hose connectivity issues. Visual review confirms additional malformation in the left hand (fused/indistinct fingers) and ambiguous fin structure. Multiple limb/extremity artifacts reduce the score below the formula baseline.
key_defects: Vertical pose instead of required horizontal swimming posture
Right hand fingers fused/malformed during 'OK' gesture
Left hand digits indistinct and structurally unclear
Regulator hose lacks distinct mechanical connection point
Fin blade merges ambiguously with background

self_reflection_notes.changes_made: No changes were made to scores or reasoning. The initial assessment was verified against the Self-Reflection Checklist.
